title: Tailwatcher: regional cohort latency benchmarking, tokens/sec profiling, and regression guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Production workloads show occasional elevated tail latency that is not captured by aggregate metrics. We need a reproducible, per-cohort observability layer that ties tokens/sec, input distribution, and 95th/99th percentile latency together for each route, model variant, and cloud region.

Goal: Deliver a Tailwatcher dashboard set and regression guardrails that: (1) surfaces 95th and 99th percentile latency per route/model/region with configurable baselines, (2) shows tokens/sec and request-rate trends alongside median/tail latencies, (3) computes automated regression signals using both statistical tests and rolling-baseline comparisons, and (4) is integrated into the existing alerting/playbook flow so oncall and SRE teams can act.

Scope: This ticket covers telemetry enrichment (new percentile emitters and tokens/sec counters per endpoint), dashboard panels and explorer views, regression detector pipeline, and a deployment + runbook for enabling alerting for high-confidence regressions. Out of scope: model re-training, dedicated capacity changes, and long-term retention policy changes (those will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dashboard space exists with panels for: tokens/sec trend, median/95/99 time series, heatmap of percentiles across regions, and cohort comparator for model variants.
2) Telemetry ingestion emits percentiles per route/model/region with tags that support efficient slice queries.
3) Regression detector flags regressions with a confidence score >= 0.95 using both a nonparametric test (Mann-Whitney U or KS) and a rolling z-score baseline; false positive rate acceptable in staging.
4) Alerts created for sustained p99 regressions > configured SLO burn threshold and wired into the incident playbook.
5) Demo run: compare baseline run (last 7 days) vs synthetic stress run showing clear flagging and dashboard annotations.
6) Owners documented, and a short kickoff doc + runbook published in Confluence.
implementation_notes:
Instrumentation: add percentile emitters at aggregation layer keyed by {route, model_version, region, instance_pool}. Emit tokens/sec per request and a per-route request counter. Sampling: keep exact percentiles for windows up to 1 minute; use tDigest rollout for longer windows.

Store: use existing percentile-telemetry stream (append tags). Expose a lightweight rollup that stores median/95/99 per 1m and 5m buckets.

Detector: implement a two-stage detector: 1) statistical test on recent window vs baseline (7d) using Mann-Whitney U; 2) change-score combining effect size and traffic-weighted delta; combine into a single score with configurable threshold. Add experiment flagging to run detector in shadow mode for 48h before enabling alerts.

Dashboards: panels planned (queries are SQL/PromQL pseudocode):
- tokens_per_sec_over_time: SELECT time_bucket, sum(tokens)/sum(duration) GROUP BY route, model_version, region
- perc_time_series: SELECT time_bucket, quantile(0.5/0.95/0.99, latency) GROUP BY route, model_version, region
- percentile_heatmap: matrix of regions x routes with cell = p95 latency (last 1h)
- regression_watchlist: list of slices with score > 0.7, recent delta, and link to playback trace

Rollout: shadow detector in staging -> run bench against canary traffic generator -> validate false positive/negative behavior -> flip to alerting in prod with quiet window and pager thresholding.

Dependencies: requires coordination with batching team to ensure tokens/sec counters include batched requests and with infra to add minor telemetry quota for new emitters.
comments: 2026-02-25 — Triage: flagged by SRE after two customer incidents where p99 spikes coincided with bursty token rates. Aisha created initial design doc and sketch. Refer: confluence/perf/tailwatcher-kickoff (internal).

2026-03-02 — Design review with observability and batching teams. Agreed to use tDigest for 5m and exact single-minute percentiles for initial rollout. Action: Carlos to draft detector algorithm and queries.
2026-03-05 — Engineering spike: implemented prototype percentile emitter on dev cluster; small overhead (~0.8% CPU). PR: github.com/redwood/infer-runtime/pull/1287 (prototype).

2026-03-09 — Bench run: synthetic workload that ramps tokens/sec to 5x baseline produced clear p99 separation; detector in shadow mode scored regressions with 0.98 confidence for target slices. Logs and results uploaded: drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/TailwatcherBenchResults (internal).

2026-03-10 — Next: finalize dashboard templates, create alerting rules, schedule canary shadow run in prod traffic for 48h. Need oncall to approve quiet thresholds. Carlos requested 0.5 FTE from SRE for rollout week.
